topics.label: The Water Cycle
facts: The water cycle is the journey water takes between Earth and the sky.
The Sun's heat turns water from seas and lakes into vapour, which is called evaporation.
When water vapour cools high in the sky, it turns into tiny drops and forms clouds, which is called condensation.
When the drops get heavy, they fall as rain, which is called precipitation.

choices: The journey water takes between Earth and the sky
questions.fact: Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as rain, and collects again.

questions.q: What is it called when the Sun turns liquid water into vapour?
questions.fact: Evaporation is when heat turns liquid water into invisible water vapour.

questions.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and forms clouds?
questions.fact: Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid drops.

questions.q: What is falling rain an example of?
questions.fact: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

topics.label: Food Chains
facts: A food chain shows who eats whom in nature.
Plants are producers because they make their own food using sunlight.
Animals that eat plants are called herbivores, and animals that eat other animals are called carnivores.
If one part of a food chain disappears, the animals that depend on it can go hungry.

questions.q: What does a food chain show?
questions.fact: A food chain links producers and consumers in the order they are eaten.

choices: They make their own food using sunlight
questions.fact: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so they start most food chains.

questions.q: What is an animal that eats only plants called?
questions.fact: Herbivores eat plants. Carnivores eat meat, and omnivores eat both.

questions.q: In the chain grass → rabbit → fox, what eats the rabbit?
questions.fact: The fox is the predator that hunts and eats the rabbit.

topics.label: Habitats
facts: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives and finds what it needs.
A habitat gives living things food, water, shelter, and space.
Forests, deserts, oceans, and ponds are all different habitats.
Animals are adapted to their habitats: polar bears have thick fur for the cold Arctic, and camels can go without water for a long time in the desert.

choices: The place where a plant or animal lives
questions.fact: A habitat is where a living thing finds food, water, shelter, and space.

questions.q: Which of these is a habitat?
questions.fact: Forests, deserts, oceans, and ponds are natural habitats.

questions.q: How is a polar bear adapted to its habitat?
choices: It has thick fur to keep warm
It has gills to breathe under water
questions.fact: Thick fur and a layer of fat keep polar bears warm in the freezing Arctic.

questions.q: What does every habitat need to give living things?
questions.fact: Without food, water, shelter, and space, living things cannot survive.

topics.label: Forests
facts: A forest is a large area of land covered mostly by trees.
Rainforests get a lot of rain and are home to more kinds of plants and animals than almost anywhere else on Earth.
Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air and release the oxygen we breathe.
Forests help keep Earth's climate steady by storing carbon in their trees and soil.

choices: A large area of land covered mostly by trees
questions.fact: A forest is a large area where trees are the main plants.

questions.q: Why are rainforests special for wildlife?
choices: Only one kind of tree grows there
They are home to more kinds of plants and animals than almost anywhere else
questions.fact: Rainforests hold a huge share of Earth's plant and animal species.

questions.q: What do trees release into the air?
questions.fact: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which we breathe.

questions.q: How do forests help Earth's climate?
choices: By storing carbon in trees and soil
questions.fact: Forests store carbon, which helps keep the climate steady.
